_readme: Every `secrets.NAME` and `vars.NAME` this repository's workflows read, and what
each one is. cli/tools/sync-pin.test.js fails when a workflow reads a name that
is not here, and when a name here is read by no workflow.
This file exists because of libviprs-org#72. `ci.yml` checked libviprs-cli out
with `secrets.SYNC_CLI_TOKEN || github.token` and SYNC_CLI_TOKEN had never been
created. The expression resolved to github.token on every run that ever ran,
libviprs-cli is public, so the checkout worked and no run reported anything. The
file read as though a private-repo path was configured, and the first person to
want that path would have found out from a red run. libviprs-org#63 is the same
shape one rung worse: CLI_COUNTERPART_REV was never set either, and an unset
variable resolves to the empty string, which actions/checkout reads as `the
default branch`.
A token cannot be checked from the log. A real run masks it: the sync job's
checkout prints `token: ***` whether the value came from a secret or from
github.token, so nothing on that line tells you which route the run took. A ref
is not masked, and the same step prints `ref: 23f85a8c...` in the clear. That
asymmetry is where the two `kind`s below come from.
kinds:
required            the name is set, and the workflow must read it plainly.
A `||` fallback is refused: it turns a missing credential
into a step that quietly does something else.
optional-announced  a secret the workflow may read as `secrets.X || <other>`,
on the condition that some step in the same file says in
the log which of the two routes the run took, and warns on
the fallback arm. `announced_by` names that step, and the
guard goes and finds it.
optional-visible    a variable the workflow may read as `vars.X || <other>`.
No announcement, because the value it overrides is echoed
unmasked in the step's own `with:` block, so a run that
took the override says so by itself.
`secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN` and `github.token` are the platform's own and need no
entry; the guard knows them and refuses an entry for them.

CLI_RESYNC_TOKEN.announced_by: Say which PR-creation route this run is on
why: cli-resync.yml opens the re-sync pull request. GITHUB_TOKEN cannot open one
here while the repository's `Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull
requests` switch is off, so the workflow takes a fine-grained PAT when one is
set and falls back to github.token when it is not. The two routes really do
behave differently (a PAT push starts ci.yml on the sync branch and a
GITHUB_TOKEN push does not), which is why the fallback is worth having at all
and why the run has to say which one it is on.
It is NOT set today. Creating it is an owner action; libviprs-org#68 wrote
down both routes and neither has been taken yet.
A one-off override for the revision the `sync` gate checks libviprs-cli out
at. It used to be the whole pin and was never set, which is libviprs-org#63:
the gate compared the frozen copy against whatever libviprs-cli main happened
to be that morning. The committed file cli/rust/COUNTERPART_REV is the pin now
and this survives only as the override.
It needs no route announcement because it cannot hide. The `Resolve the
pinned counterpart revision` step echoes the file's value, and the checkout
step's own `with:` block echoes the ref it actually used, unmasked, two lines
later. A run that took the override shows both numbers and they disagree.
